Draw splice junction arcs on annotation or coverage panels

Source: R/geom-junction.R
geom_junction.Rd

geom_junction() connects genomic donor and acceptor anchors with an upward arc. Map read counts to label and linewidth to show splice evidence. Counts describe junction support, not full transcript abundance.

Usage

geom_junction(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  height = 0.6,
  label_size = 2.5,
  label_family = "",
  label_vjust = -0.3,
  panel = c("annotation", "coverage"),
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments. Required aesthetics are x, xend, and y. Optional aesthetics include yend, track, height, label, hjust, linewidth, colour, linetype, and alpha. Use splice-boundary anchors in the annotation coordinate system. Labels default to centered horizontal justification (hjust = 0.5); map or set hjust to reposition crowded labels.

height

Positive, finite rise above the line between the endpoints at their displayed x midpoint, in the selected panel's y units, default 0.6. The curve's maximum may lie away from the midpoint when yend differs from y. Alternatively map height to give junctions different rises. An explicitly supplied constant overrides the mapping. The layer reserves vertical room for the arc and an additional quarter of its rise when a label is present.

label_size

Label text size in mm, default 2.5.

label_family

Label font family.

label_vjust

Vertical label justification relative to the curve at the displayed x midpoint, default -0.3. Labels inherit the arc colour and alpha.

panel

Target panel, either "annotation" (the default) or "coverage". Use "coverage" to align arcs with a BigWig track. Map track to the corresponding coverage track and express y, yend, and height in its signal units. Junctions reserve vertical room under ordinary scale training, but do not affect signal-derived automatic coverage limits. Explicit or automatic scale_panel_coverage() limits remain authoritative; choose suitable arc positions or explicit limits to retain headroom.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

With scale_x_ggexon_genomic(), endpoints consume the exon-trained map and arcs are generated afterwards. Labels sit halfway between the displayed endpoints, on the curve. The layer does not train exon boundaries. In Syn-backed facet_genomics() plots, panel selects the annotation or coverage panel matching each junction's track. It also works in ordinary ggplot2 plots, where panel does not create a separate panel. Map yend to anchor the end independently; it defaults to y. The baseline interpolates linearly between the endpoint heights in displayed x coordinates, and the curve rises above it for either endpoint order.

See also

geom_coverage(), geom_exon2(), scale_x_ggexon_genomic()

Examples

junctions <- data.frame(donor = c(100, 100), acceptor = c(300, 700),
  y = c(1, 2), reads = c(45, 21))
ggplot2::ggplot(junctions, ggplot2::aes(x = donor, xend = acceptor, y = y)) +
  geom_junction(ggplot2::aes(label = reads, linewidth = reads))
